cost_sensitivity.why: Sharpe and DSR are not re-priced: they require the per-bar net series, which the record stores only as aggregates. Net, fees, turnover and the net-positive count are exact because fees are linear in turnover.

dispersion_method: within resolution: a daily Sharpe and a 15-minute Sharpe estimate different quantities, so the hurdle is built from the dispersion at the row's own resolution while the trial count stays the whole disclosed family

limitations: the fixed maps have no trainable parameters; the parameterised map is fitted on 12 grid points per dataset and that search is charged to the deflation, so the fit is not quoted as a lone hypothesis

the closed form prod_i cos(alpha_i x_i + beta_i) means every map here is classically computable in O(n) floating-point operations; the statevector simulation is the definition of the circuit, not the cheapest evaluation, so no advantage is claimed
ten datasets across two resolutions (six daily panels, four 15-minute snapshots), no slippage beyond the declared fee, and no live feed

the holdout is temporal and consumed once: a slice whose candidate loses money after fees is burned in the durable ledger and cannot be re-entered, so this record is not regenerable from the same slices by design

the holding period is one bar, so the 15-minute rows annualise a Sharpe estimated from roughly ten days of bars and should be read as a resolution comparison, not a ten-day backtest of a trading business

trial_ledger.note: every grid point is one recorded trial, so the fit is charged at the size of its search exactly as the threshold sweep is
